results.summary_before: This design converts a 4-bit binary input into a 7-segment display pattern using a simple combinational circuit of OR and AND gates. It is tested by setting the first four switches to a binary value from 0 to 15 and observing the display. No external hardware beyond the switches and a 7-segment display is required. Silicon testing confirmed correct operation for digits 0 through 9, but values 10 to 15 do not display, which the testers note may be intentional but would be nicer as hexadecimal.

results.summary_before: This design combines a tapped ring oscillator with a glitchless clock source switch, allowing selection between two external clocks. To test the oscillator, one of the three inverted taps is fed back to input 0, while the clock switch is tested by using input 1 to select between clock0 and clock1, with the selected clock appearing on output 3. No external hardware beyond clock sources and feedback wiring is required. The documentation is concise but describes both functional blocks and their test procedure clearly.

results.summary_before: This Verilog design generates a sawtooth waveform for audio by incrementing a counter from 0 to 25,000,000 and feeding the value into a PDM modulator, with the frequency set by a 4-bit left-shift amount. It is tested by adding an RC low-pass filter with a cutoff around 30 kHz to output pin 7, which can be probed with an oscilloscope or connected to an audio amplifier to listen to the result. The design outputs both PCM bits and a PDM stream, and follows the Tiny Tapeout audio pinout recommendation. It is notable for being a straightforward audio waveform generator that requires external filtering and amplification to be useful.

The project is a minor variation of an existing design and includes links to the original Wokwi project.

results.summary_before: This is an analog relaxation oscillator designed to produce a ~2 MHz signal, with an inverter providing a full-swing square wave output. The analog output is on one pin and the digital square wave on another. Silicon tests show it oscillates at around 1 MHz, but the frequency is highly sensitive to loading on the analog pin, and a 10k pulldown must be removed for oscillation. The author notes that loading the analog output can stop oscillation due to the lack of a buffer.

results.summary_before: This is a chess move generator implemented in SystemVerilog. It uses a 256-bit chessboard and a 64-bit square-enable mask to compute attacks and arbitrate the most promising move. The design is intended to be driven by an external RP2040 microprocessor, as the chip lacks the space to run the full game logic. It is tested using a provided test suite.
